Grouped integer/predicate values written to F32 require conversion rather than storing carrier bits; ordinary mixed writes are not covered by plain F32 add anchors.
An integer-valued floating literal must round as its declared F32 type; catches a wrong predicate/value independently of transcendental accuracy.
Negative intermediate division/remainder affects addresses, where approximation is invalid; differs from nonnegative constant stride indexing in anchors.
Width-four loads have offsets 1 and 2 plus an odd row count; tests legal scalar fallback instead of assuming aligned vectors.
Small integer-valued F32 transport observes the outer binding after a nested Tile. Exact data movement is not an arithmetic precision restriction.
An inner loop axis shadows a Tile axis; subsequent addressing must restore the proper owner. A different lexical entry/exit from nested-Tile-only case30.
Nested Tiles have unequal extents; each needs its own guard and continuation. Case30's restoration alone cannot establish correct masking.
Inactive lanes must contribute one to a product. Actual inputs are exactly representable unit values, so tolerance does not prohibit valid reassociation.
Inactive lanes must not contribute zero to a minimum over positive values; distinct operation from product/max.
Inactive lanes must not contribute zero to a maximum over negative values; distinct sign/identity from minimum.
A skipped loop must preserve the entry value of a tree-reduction carrier; tree/shared behavior differs from warp-only case39.
A skipped loop must preserve a warp-reduction carrier. Exact small integers make this a state-lifetime check rather than summation-order stress.
An inner Init must not replace an outer accumulator's binding. Small exact constants distinguish a scope error from rounding.
Dynamic shared addresses, masked 16-byte copies, zero fill and commit/wait ordering are a useful transport interaction not exercised by aligned full-tile copies alone.
A 63-of-65 active K range with conditional updates and inherited seeds tests tile/tail legality at matmul tolerances, not serial bit identity.
Width257 crosses more than one cooperative column slice; bounded logits and published-like tolerances distinguish normalization/tail bugs without exact arithmetic.
A logical axis named _gid and block80 expose physical/logical ID confusion plus a partial physical warp; different subgroup geometry from ordinary CTA128 anchors.
A scalar Load declaration must not overwrite an outer value used by later indexing; exact integer transport isolates the lifetime defect.
A grouped Load's addresses/RHS values must be captured before any destination name is rebound; scalar-shadow alone does not test simultaneity.
An inner declaration and an inherited accumulator update have different owners. Small exact arithmetic makes scope, not rounding, the acceptance condition.
A partially active CTA must execute finite uniform nested loops consistently around collectives; memory masking alone does not preserve barrier participation.
Child dot folds reuse ancestor score names, while KEY-owned totals must escape. Small bounded integer operands keep reassociation/FMA free of rounding obstructions.
The generated one-row small reduction uses a different schedule from published rmsnorm. Published-like tolerances and ordinary inputs earn generic-path coverage.
Rows of length3 force short-row/tail behavior absent from published length512 normalization; ordinary inputs use the same style of output tolerance.
A thin dimension and K31 test a different atomic contraction geometry, resets and tail handling from the rectangular published fixture.
A serial width31 row exercises generic max/sum/normalization rather than only the cooperative online recognizer. Tolerance matches published softmax.
Three kernels require intermediate buffers, ordered launches and distinct positional ABIs. A single fused attention kernel cannot replace this coverage.
Lead2/slots3 with extent7 observes wraparound and dead final lookahead. Small integer-valued sums impose no realistic FP-order penalty.
Extent2 equals prefill lead2: the steady-state path disappears while initial stages remain live. Different boundary from extent1 and extent7.
Step2 with nondivisible bound tests logical iteration count versus raw axis extent in ring rotation and wait accounting.
Padding is deliberately read later, so a compiler cannot delete a lookahead copy solely because its arithmetic iteration is dead; an effect/visibility check.
Extent1 is shorter than lead2 and must suppress invalid initial prefill, unlike extent2 where both prefill stages are valid.
Extent9, inherited seeds -5/7 and small integer operands yield results up to36. Exactness is harmless for these actual values and catches seed/tail errors without forcing general serial rounding.
Row stride258 differs in alignment from128 and small operands remain exact. This earns a separate runtime/scalar-fallback check from71.
Bounded input, D16 and a complete key segment exercise cooperative score reuse at normal tolerances beyond published shapes.
The19-by19 key/query shape with D7 exercises fallback and masked partial segments, unlike75's complete segment.
Two bounded queries must retain separate maxima/denominators. Reusing a normalization across distinct queries changes the function, not just rounding.
Despite the cancellation label, actual q/kt magnitudes are below0.21. Non-unit seeded coefficients and width32 test recognition legality with an ordinary-domain error budget.
Keys65 cross a width32 boundary with non-unit coefficients. The original full32 witness80 cannot establish last-segment masking.
Partial D7 geometry plus non-unit coefficients combines a fallback path with coefficient-sensitive semantics; standard-coefficient fallback76 is not its replacement.
Two actually equivalent normalization graphs should remain equivalent when values are reused; distinct-query case79 tests the opposite condition and does not replace this.
Same lifetime bug as57, but subgroup width8 selects a distinct lane grouping from width16. Small exact integer data do not constrain FP approximation.
Multi-trip ordinary and strided loops distinguish local seeded declarations, exported current-loop folds and inherited updates. All actual expected values are small exact integers.
Width127 tests a masked single slice. The multi-slice257 case47 exercises different last-slice conditions and is not a dominance proof.
Direct Loop and nested StridedLoop56 use different statement dispatch and barrier entry; preserve both code paths with small exact integer sums.
Lead3/slots4 adds an initial publication/wait stage relative to lead2/slots3. This is an additional scheduling boundary, not just another seed.
Width-one scalar adds over4099 values test the final element and partial Tile without the expression machinery in15 or grouped-vector path in91.
Grouped width2 add with2049 values has one leftover element; published aligned width2 and width4 row-oriented case25 do not exercise this boundary.
Collective scratch/right-hand names must restore outer values. Data and expected sums are small exact integers, so the256 wrong outputs are state corruption, not acceptable approximation.

Pure renaming of a logical axis to tid must preserve ordinary attention at its unchanged tolerance. It directly catches4095 wrong outputs in a currently optimized path, with no adversarial numeric data.
